ASSESSMENT — Obsolete MCP HMAC secret infrastructure (`MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY` / `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key`)

Read-only assessment. No infrastructure or documentation was changed (see AC7 at end). Method: full-tree grep, `src/tests/scripts` and compose consumer sweeps, git-blame of introducing commits, and cross-read of ADR 0049 + `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md`.

== AC1 — Complete reference inventory (producer / transport / consumer / doc) ==

`grep -rn "MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY\|mcp-hmac-signing-key" .` (excluding `.git/`, `.venv/`) — every match classified:

PRODUCER (creates the secret slot):
- `infra/terraform/ssm.tf:21` — declares SSM SecureString slot `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key` in `local.rebar_secret_params` (created as the `CHANGEME` placeholder; `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`).

TRANSPORT (SSM -> env file; no consumer downstream):
- `infra/terraform/user_data.sh:92` — cloud-init PARAMS map `["/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key"]="MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY"`; written to `/etc/rebar/.env` (0600) at boot, CHANGEME-fail-fast. NOTE: `/etc/rebar/.env` is NOT the compose `env_file` (compose uses `infra/compose/.env`); this host `.env` has no identified consumer.
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:13` — doc-comment mapping `-> MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY (verdict signing)`.
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:82` — `mcp_hmac_signing_key="$(get_param mcp-hmac-signing-key)"`.
- `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:148` — writes `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY=${mcp_hmac_signing_key}` into `infra/compose/.env`.

CONSUMER (runtime reader of the value):
- NONE. Evidence:
  - `grep -rn "MCP_HMAC" src/ tests/ scripts/` -> no matches (exit 1).
  - `grep -rn "MCP_HMAC\|mcp-hmac" infra/compose/` -> no matches (exit 1); `docker-compose.yml` never names it. Both the `reviewbot` and `opcert` services load `infra/compose/.env` via `env_file:`, so the variable is INJECTED into their process environment, but no application code reads `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`.
  - rebar's own symmetric HMAC signing (`src/rebar/_signing_hmac.py:70`) reads `REBAR_SIGNING_KEY` or the gitignored `<tracker>/.signing-key` — NEVER `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`. The generic HMAC utility that "remains available" (per the migration doc) does not read this env var either.
  - Current verdict signing is done by the `opcert` service with the Ed25519 op-cert private key at `/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key` (`REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`, `docker-compose.yml:285`). No HMAC secret participates.

DOC (operator/reference documentation):
- `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md:57` — IaC secret inventory list item.
- `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:105` — operator SSM table row, "Consumed by: verdict signing".
- `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:117` — named in the fetched-subset prose.
- `infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md:102` — restore runbook comment listing secrets to repopulate.

EVAL/TEST CORPUS (frozen fixtures quoting this ticket's own text — not producer/transport/consumer; tracked):
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/adjudication_corpus.jsonl` (1 occurrence).
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl` (1 occurrence).

LOCAL TELEMETRY (git-ignored, transient — generated by THIS assessment's own `review-plan` run, which fed the ticket text to the plan-reviewer):
- `.rebar/usage.jsonl` (4x `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`, 3x `mcp-hmac-signing-key`) — `git check-ignore` confirms ignored; not tracked, not infra.

== AC2 — Originating closed tickets + superseding decisions ==

Introduced by (git -S blame of the matching lines):
- `rot-tarn-revel` (`5bfc-c3f8-72d6-40dc`) — "infra: S1 — Terraform base (... SSM secrets ...)": created `ssm.tf` slot, `user_data.sh` map entry, and the `docs/adr/0012` list item.
- `smelly-pane-bolt` (`786b-190d-5e3a-4194`) — "infra: S2 — Deploy Gerrit + rebar MCP (docker-compose) behind nginx + TLS": added the `fetch-secrets.sh` mapping labeled "verdict signing".
- `pesky-eye-pad` (`3178-7e4c-b571-473c`) — "infra: S7 — End-to-end proof + backup/restore drill + monitoring + runbooks": added the `provision-restore.md` runbook mention.
- `ship-strip-sugar` (`1628-ad81-0831-46a2`) — "Client walkthrough: self-host Gerrit + rebar review-bot on AWS to gate GitHub": added the `gerrit-aws-setup.md` operator table.

Superseded by:
- ADR 0049 (`docs/adr/0049-opcert-asymmetric.md`) — replaced the per-clone symmetric-HMAC verdict signing (a shared secret any verifier could forge) with asymmetric, environment-attributed Ed25519 `rebar.opcert.v1` operation certificates (plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close).
- `docs/migrations/hmac-opcert-removal.md` — the expand -> contract migration that removes the legacy HMAC scheme for the two op-cert kinds (`plan-review`, `completion-verifier`); after the contract phase (story 8f1d) those kinds resolve ONLY the asymmetric `sshsig` op-cert scheme.
- Discovered-from: `aventurine-sharpcut-vampirebat` (`89af-b080-1216-4229`) — "F09 align operation-certificate guidance with asymmetric signing" (the F09 sweep that surfaced this orphan).

== Conclusion ==

`MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY` / `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key` is ORPHANED dead secret infrastructure: it has a producer (the SSM slot) and transport (into two `.env` files) but ZERO consumers. Its sole documented purpose ("verdict signing") was superseded by asymmetric op-certs (ADR 0049); the shipped verdict-signing path uses the Ed25519 op-cert key, not any HMAC secret. It is safe to remove. Removal is a deployment/security change and — per this ticket's constraint "Do not remove infrastructure before operator approval" — is NOT executed here; it should proceed as a separate operator-approved follow-up.

== AC3 — Compatibility consequences of removal ==

- No runtime/application consumer breaks: nothing reads the variable. reviewbot/opcert verdict signing (op-cert Ed25519 key) is unaffected. Dropping the injected-but-unused var from the containers' environment is a no-op.
- Net improvement: `user_data.sh` currently REQUIRES the slot to be non-`CHANGEME` or a fresh boot dies (CHANGEME-fail-fast). Removing it deletes a boot-time coupling to a secret that does nothing.
- Atomicity requirement: removal MUST be atomic across the producer and BOTH transports. If the terraform slot is destroyed while `user_data.sh` / `fetch-secrets.sh` still call `get-parameter`/`get_param` on that leaf, the fetch fails and BOTH scripts fail-fast (abort boot / refuse to write `.env`). Do not remove the slot before removing the two script references (or remove the references first — see two-phase option below).

== AC4 — Rollback consequences of removal ==

- No supported rollback target consumes `MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY`. ADR 0049's required-environment posture is opt-in/off by default and the op-cert path is the shipped mechanism; there is no supported rollback that re-introduces HMAC verdict signing needing this secret. The HMAC scheme for op-cert kinds is contracted/removed (`hmac-opcert-removal.md`).
- Redeploying a pre-ADR-0049 image is not a live/supported target. If an operator ever needed it, re-creating the slot is a one-line terraform re-add plus `aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite` (cheap, value-preserving), so rollback is recoverable but manual, not automatic.
- Safer intermediate that preserves trivial rollback: FIRST stop fetching/injecting (remove the `user_data.sh` + `fetch-secrets.sh` references) while RETAINING the terraform slot for one release; destroy the slot only after confirming nothing regressed.

== AC5 — Secret-rotation consequences of removal ==

- Today operators are instructed to populate/rotate this secret (`gerrit-aws-setup.md`; `provision-restore.md` lists it among secrets to repopulate on restore). Because nothing consumes it, rotation is pure toil with zero security effect — rotating it changes no signature. Removal ELIMINATES a rotation obligation and removes a misleading "verdict signing" entry from the operator rotation checklist and restore runbook.
- Residual risk if RETAINED: operators keep provisioning, KMS-storing, and rotating a live-looking secret that grants nothing (audit noise + confusion), and its presence implies HMAC verdict signing is still active, contradicting ADR 0049.

== AC6 — Bounded remediation proposal (removal; requires operator approval; NOT executed) ==

Exact file list (6 tracked files; zero code, zero test changes):
1. `infra/terraform/ssm.tf` — delete the `"/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key",` entry from `local.rebar_secret_params` (line 21).
2. `infra/terraform/user_data.sh` — delete the PARAMS entry `["/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key"]="MCP_HMAC_SIGNING_KEY"` (line 92).
3. `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` — delete the doc line (13), the `get_param` fetch (82), and the `.env` write line (148).
4. `docs/adr/0012-iac-foundations.md` — delete the list item (line 57), or annotate as removed/superseded-by-ADR-0049.
5. `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` — delete the operator-table row (105) and the fetched-subset mention (117).
6. `infra/runbooks/provision-restore.md` — drop `mcp-hmac-signing-key` from the repopulate-secrets comment (102).
(Leave the eval-corpus jsonl and the git-ignored `.rebar/usage.jsonl` untouched — fixtures / transient telemetry, not infra.)

Deployment steps implied:
- Terraform: `terraform plan` shows the `aws_ssm_parameter` for that leaf as to-be-destroyed; because it holds only an unused placeholder, `apply` safely removes the slot. To keep rollback headroom, do it in two applies (first drop the script references, later destroy the slot).
- Instance: next boot (or a re-run of `fetch-secrets.sh`) regenerates `.env` / `/etc/rebar/.env` without the line; no service restart semantics change (nothing consumed it); no data migration.
- Ops hygiene: one fewer SecureString/KMS object to manage; update operator rotation + restore checklists.
- Blast radius: 6 tracked files, one (or two-phase) terraform apply, zero code/test changes, no service downtime.

== AC7 — No infrastructure changed during the assessment ==

`git status --porcelain infra/ docs/` -> empty (verified before writing this comment). This assessment is read-only; any removal is deferred to an operator-approved follow-up.
